What Is Bhumi Amla Plant?

Bhumi Amla, scientifically known as Phyllanthus niruri, is a small medicinal herb widely found across India. It is commonly called Stonebreaker, Seed-under-Leaf or Gale of the Wind in English, and Bhumyamalaki in Ayurveda. The plant is traditionally valued for its potential applications in liver health, urinary health and digestive wellness. It is easily recognizable by its tiny green fruits growing underneath its small leaf-like branchlets.

What Are the Key Characteristics of Bhumi Amla?

Bhumi Amla belongs to the Phyllanthaceae family. It is a small annual herb with a slender, erect, green and branched stem and a small branched taproot system. The leaves are small, simple and arranged alternately along branchlets, appearing in two rows. The flowers are tiny and greenish-yellow, found near the leaf axils. The fruits are small round capsules growing underneath the leaf-like branchlets, enclosing small seeds.

Why Is Bhumi Amla Important in Indian Traditions?

Bhumi Amla, known as Bhumyamalaki in Ayurveda, is a valued medicinal herb in Indian households. It commonly grows during the rainy season in gardens, agricultural fields and moist open areas across India. It is traditionally used in herbal preparations for liver-related complaints, urinary discomfort, digestive complaints, jaundice, fever and skin preparations. However, these uses are based on traditional knowledge and research of varying quality; they are not established treatments for human diseases.

What Are the Medicinal Uses of Bhumi Amla in Ayurveda?

In Ayurveda, different parts of Bhumi Amla are used in herbal preparations. The traditional uses include:

  • Liver health: Traditionally used in preparations for liver-related complaints.
  • Urinary health: Used in traditional preparations for urinary discomfort.
  • Kidney stone research: Investigated for possible effects on urinary stone formation and passage.
  • Digestive health: Traditionally used for digestive complaints.
  • Jaundice: Historically used in traditional preparations for jaundice, but it is not a proven treatment.
  • Skin health: Used in certain traditional herbal preparations.
  • Fever: Traditionally used in some herbal remedies for fever-related complaints.

These are traditional uses and research interests, not established treatments for human diseases.

What Are the Health Benefits of Bhumi Amla?

Most of what is known about Bhumi Amla comes from laboratory and animal studies, not large human trials. A 2016 review in the Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmacology summarised research on its liver-protective, antiviral, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, much of it linked to lignans such as phyllanthin. These are promising leads, not proven treatments.

Some lab studies have looked at effects on blood sugar, but Bhumi Amla is not an established diabetes treatment, and anyone on diabetes medicine should check with their doctor before taking it.

What Does Human Research Show?

Kidney stones: A 2020 meta-analysis found only two controlled human studies; together they showed modest reductions in stone size and number, and the authors called the evidence limited (PubMed 32333735). In a 2006 trial of 150 patients after lithotripsy, 93.5% of those taking a Phyllanthus niruri extract were stone-free versus 83.3% without it (PubMed 16890682).

Hepatitis B: A Cochrane review of 16 trials found insufficient evidence to support or refute Phyllanthus for chronic hepatitis B (Cochrane CD008960). It is not a substitute for antiviral treatment.

What Active Chemical Compounds Are Found in Bhumi Amla?

Bhumi Amla contains several naturally occurring phytochemicals:

  • Phyllanthin: A lignan studied for potential liver-protective activity.
  • Hypophyllanthin: A naturally occurring lignan.
  • Niranthin: A lignan found in certain Phyllanthus species.
  • Flavonoids: Plant compounds with antioxidant properties.
  • Tannins: Naturally occurring polyphenolic compounds.
  • Gallic acid: A phenolic compound.
  • Ellagic acid: A natural antioxidant compound.
  • Terpenoids: Plant compounds studied for biological activities.

These compounds are being investigated for their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and other potential properties.

How Is Bhumi Amla Used in Traditional Preparations?

The whole plant is traditionally used in various Ayurvedic preparations:

A. Fresh plant: Collect a correctly identified, healthy plant. Wash thoroughly with clean water. Traditionally, the whole plant is used in herbal preparations. Do not consume it raw without professional guidance.

B. Leaf juice: Fresh leaves are traditionally washed and crushed. Juice is extracted for traditional herbal preparations. There is no universally established safe medicinal dosage.

C. Whole-plant powder: The plant is cleaned and dried hygienically. The dried material is ground into powder. It is used in certain traditional herbal formulations.

Typical label dose: Packaged churna in India commonly suggests 3 to 5 g mixed in warm water, once or twice a day after meals (for example, the Ayurved Power label, checked 22 November 2026). That is the maker's suggestion, not a clinically established dose, so follow your doctor or Ayurvedic practitioner, and avoid long courses without advice.

D. Herbal preparations: Bhumi Amla is included in some Ayurvedic preparations. Medicinal use should be guided by a qualified healthcare professional.

Important: Do not use Bhumi Amla to treat kidney stones, jaundice or liver disease without medical assessment.

What Are the Environmental Benefits of Bhumi Amla?

Bhumi Amla's small flowers provide resources for tiny insects, supporting biodiversity. It is an important herb in Ayurvedic medicine and provides natural phytochemicals for pharmaceutical research. It commonly grows in tropical and subtropical environments and is useful for documenting India's traditional medicinal plant diversity.

Where Else in the World Does Bhumi Amla Grow?

Phyllanthus niruri is native to tropical and subtropical regions. Besides India, it grows in other parts of South Asia, Southeast Asia, and tropical regions of the Americas and Africa. In many regions it is known as a common weed, while in traditional medicine systems it is valued for herbal preparations.

How Much Does Bhumi Amla Cost in India?

Fresh Bhumi Amla plants and dried whole-plant material are sold by local herbal vendors and ayurvedic stores. Packaged 100 g Bhumi Amla churna (powder) sold online in India cost about ₹90 to ₹200 as of 22 November 2026: for example, Tansukh churna at ₹90 (MRP ₹100) on 1mg and Ayurved Power at ₹199 (MRP ₹250) on its own store. Prices change often and vary by brand and city. Compare the price per 100 g and check the label before buying.

Labels to check in India: Bhumi Amla juice, powder and capsules sold as food must carry an FSSAI licence or registration number. Products sold as Ayurvedic medicines are regulated under the Ministry of AYUSH and should show a drug licence number. Watch for added sugar in juices and murabba-style preparations.

A Note for Readers Outside India

In the US, UK, Canada and Australia, Bhumi Amla is mostly sold as a dried powder, capsule or "Stonebreaker" supplement, and fresh plant material is less commonly available. In the US, supplements are not approved by the FDA to treat or prevent any disease, and in the UK most such products are sold as food supplements rather than licensed medicines. The same safety advice applies everywhere: talk to your doctor before taking concentrated extracts, especially if you take diabetes or blood-pressure medicines.

What Safety Precautions Should You Follow?

Important health precautions:

  • Do not consume unidentified wild plants.
  • Avoid excessive consumption of raw plant material or concentrated extracts.
  • It may potentially affect blood sugar and blood pressure.
  • Consult a healthcare professional if taking diabetes or blood-pressure medicines.
  • People taking blood-thinning medicines should seek medical advice before using concentrated extracts.
  • Pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid medicinal use unless advised by a healthcare professional.
  • People with liver or kidney disease should not self-medicate with this plant.
  • Do not replace prescribed medicines with Bhumi Amla.

Human safety and effective dosage have not been adequately established.

Conclusion

Bhumi Amla (Phyllanthus niruri), commonly known as Stonebreaker Plant, is an important traditional medicinal herb belonging to the family Phyllanthaceae. It is widely found in India and is commonly recognized by its small leaves and tiny fruits growing underneath the leaf-like branches.

The plant contains several bioactive compounds, including phyllanthin, hypophyllanthin, flavonoids and tannins. It is traditionally used for liver health, urinary complaints, digestive health and other herbal preparations. Its potential antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and liver-related properties make it valuable for medicinal plant research. However, further high-quality human clinical studies are necessary to establish its medicinal effectiveness and safety.

In simple words: Bhumi Amla is a small medicinal herb traditionally valued for liver and urinary health. It is popularly known as the Stonebreaker Plant, but its ability to treat kidney stones or liver diseases has not been conclusively proven.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Bhumi Amla safe for daily consumption?

There is no universally established safe daily dose. Fresh plant material or whole-plant powder can be used in small amounts as part of traditional preparations, but concentrated supplements should only be taken under the guidance of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner or doctor.

Can pregnant women use Bhumi Amla?

Pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid medicinal use of Bhumi Amla unless advised by a healthcare professional, as human safety and effective dosage have not been adequately established.

What conditions is Bhumi Amla traditionally used for?

Bhumi Amla is traditionally used in Ayurveda for liver-related complaints, urinary discomfort, digestive complaints, jaundice, fever, skin health and kidney stone support. These uses are based on traditional knowledge and research of varying quality; they are not established treatments for human diseases.

Which parts of the Bhumi Amla plant are used?

The whole plant, leaves, roots and fruits are useful parts. Fresh leaves are used for juice, the whole plant is dried and powdered, and fruits are used in traditional preparations.

Can Bhumi Amla replace prescribed medical treatment?

No. Do not use Bhumi Amla as a replacement for prescribed treatment. People with liver or kidney disease should not self-medicate with this plant, and people with chronic medical conditions or taking regular medicines should consult a healthcare professional before using concentrated extracts.

Where does Bhumi Amla grow in India?

Bhumi Amla commonly grows during the rainy season in India. It can be found in gardens, agricultural fields and moist open areas across tropical and subtropical regions of the country.
